name: NSW-Victoria Interconnector Separation
summary: Severe bushfire conditions in the Snowy Mountains region caused multiple 330 kV line trips, leading to separation of the NSW and Victorian power systems via the VIC-NSW interconnector. This was one of the most significant power system events during the Black Summer bushfires.
source: AEMO Power System Operating Incident Report - NSW/VIC Separation January 2020

timeline.event: Bushfire conditions intensify in Snowy Mountains region
Upper Tumut to Canberra 330 kV line trips due to fire-related fault
N-1 constraints invoked for Snowy region
Murray to Upper Tumut 330 kV line trips
Lower Tumut to Canberra line trips due to cascading protection
NSW-VIC interconnector separation occurs. Victoria and NSW systems now operating independently
Emergency frequency control activated in both regions
First 330 kV line restored after fire subsides
All Snowy region lines returned to service

lines.Upper Tumut-Canberra 3 330kV: Not exact match - closest: 'Lower Tumut to Canberra'

aemoNameMapping.notes: Some Snowy region interconnector lines (especially VIC-NSW ties through the mountains) may not be fully represented in GA public data. Substation names match well. The Murray-Upper Tumut internal Snowy Hydro connections may be classified differently.

notes: This was one of the most significant power system security events during the Black Summer bushfires. The separation of the two largest NEM regions (NSW and VIC) required careful resynchronisation. Snowy Hydro generators played a critical role in maintaining frequency control during the separation.
